items.text: HDFC SKY (1 day ago) confirmed: the Iran war deteriorated sharply on Tuesday as the United States conducted fresh strikes in southern Iran's Hormozgan province targeting missile sites and boats attempting to lay mines, prompting Tehran's foreign ministry to declare the attacks a "gross violation" of the tenuous ceasefire that had been in place for nearly seven weeks. The Hormozgan province is the Iranian coastal region immediately adjacent to the Strait of Hormuz — it is the operational base for IRGC Hormuz activities. The targets: missile sites (pre-emptive denial of future missile attacks) and boats attempting to lay mines (protecting the de-mining process that is part of the WaPo/Iran FM MOU framework). The US legal justification: self-defence under existing war powers, protecting freedom of navigation. Iran's response: gross ceasefire violation — the same language used on Day 80 when the UAE was attacked. The MOU framework (WaPo + Iran FM confirmed) is still valid architecturally — but Iran calling this a violation threatens to unravel it.

items.bold: WHY THE US STRUCK: Boats laying NEW MINES = direct threat to MOU de-mining architecture. US pre-empted to protect Hormuz reopening framework.
items.text: The strategic logic of Tuesday's US strikes: The WaPo/Iran FM confirmed MOU framework requires Hormuz to be de-mined as a first-phase deliverable. CENTCOM Admiral Cooper had confirmed 90% of mines destroyed. Iranian boats were attempting to lay NEW mines in the Strait — directly undermining the de-mining process that is core to the MOU. The US targeted: (1) missile sites in Hormozgan (prevent future missile attacks on commercial vessels during de-mining), (2) boats laying mines (protect de-mining of Hormuz from fresh contamination). This is not the US breaking the ceasefire — it is the US enforcing the conditions required for the MOU to work. Iran's perspective: any US strike on Iranian territory = ceasefire violation. US perspective: protecting ships from fresh mines = legitimate self-defence. The fundamental tension: who defines what constitutes a ceasefire violation in a conflict where neither side has a formal status-of-forces agreement.

items.bold: MOU FRAMEWORK STATUS: Still architecturally valid. WaPo + Iran FM both confirmed. But Iran "gross violation" language threatens to unravel signing timeline.
items.text: The MOU framework remains confirmed by: (1) Washington Post senior admin official (May 25): 60-day ceasefire extension + Hormuz de-mined + reopened. (2) Iran foreign ministry (CNBC): MOU as first phase, broader talks 30-60 days. (3) Pakistan + Qatar + Witkoff mediator architecture (FT). None of these sources have retracted their confirmation. The Tuesday US strikes have not formally collapsed the framework. But Iran's "gross violation" declaration creates a diplomatic crisis: Iran may refuse to sign the MOU while the US is conducting fresh strikes. The MOU signing was described as "imminent" — Tuesday's events may have delayed it by days to weeks. Critical question: will Pakistan and Qatar mediators contain the "gross violation" declaration and return both sides to the MOU signing table?

assessment.body:
Wednesday 9:15 AM IST. Day 89. The deal was signed — then wasn't.

WHAT HAPPENED TUESDAY
The US conducted fresh strikes in Iran's Hormozgan province:
→ Missile sites (prevent future attacks on commercial vessels during de-mining)
→ Boats attempting to lay new mines (protect the MOU de-mining architecture)
Iran's response: declared it a "gross violation of the ceasefire."
Brent: +3.6% to $99.58. One of the sharpest single-session crude swings in weeks.
India: expiry-day selloff. Nifty fell below 24,000.

WHY THE US STRUCK
Boats laying NEW mines in Hormuz = direct threat to the MOU de-mining process.
The WaPo framework requires Hormuz to be de-mined in Phase 1.
Iran trying to re-mine Hormuz while negotiating de-mining = sabotage of the MOU architecture.
US perspective: self-defence + protecting the deal's deliverables.
Iran perspective: any strike on Iranian territory = violation.

THE CRITICAL QUESTION
Is Iran formally withdrawing from the MOU framework — or just protesting?
Three-source MOU confirmation (WaPo + Iran FM + FT) still stands.
No formal retraction confirmed as of 9:15 AM.
Pakistan + Qatar + Witkoff mediators still active.
If Iran protests-only: MOU signing resumes within days.
If Iran withdraws: Brent $104-108, Nifty 23,400-23,600.

INDIA'S WEDNESDAY
GIFT Nifty -40.50 (23,872.50) = muted/negative open.
Expected: Nifty 23,820-23,880, Sensex ~75,900-76,100.
Volatile session — single Iran statement can move Nifty 300-500 points either direction.
PGSA applications: submit today — MOU still valid.
Kharif fertiliser: order today — delay, not cancellation.
Haji Ali protest: file today.

VERDICT: Day 89 is the morning after the deal that almost was. Monday: Brent -7%, Sensex +1,073, Nifty above 24,000 for first time. Tuesday: US strikes Hormozgan, Brent +3.6%, Nifty below 24,000, Iran calls it gross violation. The MOU framework is still architecturally valid — three independent sources confirmed it and none have retracted. The question Wednesday is whether Iran's "gross violation" language is negotiating theatre or a genuine withdrawal from the framework. That single diplomatic signal will determine Wednesday's direction for India's markets, Brent, and the Hormuz reopening timeline.
